title: e3_execution_protocol_v1
description: M5 deferred scaffold: run-experiment.mjs rejects host_cli before planning or execution, regardless of authorization; real host execution requires new P0.7/P0.8 code and approval. This is the deterministic fixture form of an E3 design. The preregistration says what would count as an answer; it deliberately does not say how to obtain one, and its placeholders (a profile name, a bare invocation mode) are not host mechanics. This artifact supplies exactly those mechanics and nothing else: which binary is launched, with which argv, under which disposable roots, against which budgets, and under which recorded human approval. Everything scientific stays where it was sealed — the arm IDs, prompt digest and held-constant fields are read back from the bound preregistration and may not be restated differently here. The launcher is a path AND a digest because a runner that resolves a name from PATH can be handed a different binary between the approval and the run; naming it makes the difference between a harness that cannot make an external call and one that merely does not. Read by run-experiment.mjs and verify-execution.sh.

preregistration.description: The sealed design this protocol executes. Its digest is checked against the bytes, so a protocol cannot quietly belong to a different experiment.

amendment.description: The approved artifact that supplied the host mechanics, when one exists separately from this protocol.

human_gate.description: An approval is a recorded decision with a digest, not a status field. `pending` is the honest default and blocks execution; nothing in the runner may set it.

launcher.description: The exact binary every arm is run through. `deterministic_fixture` answers from canned bytes and reaches no network; `host_cli` is the real host and is the only kind that can spend an external call.

launcher_script.description: When the launcher is an interpreter, the interpreter's digest says nothing about what runs — the script does. So a deterministic fixture binds its script here, it must be argv[0] of every arm, and its bytes are checked like the binary's. A `host_cli` launcher has no script: the binary IS the thing being run, and an interposed script would be an unapproved layer between the approval and the host.

budgets.description: Ceilings, not estimates. `executor_retries` is 0 because a retried arm is a second sample presented as one.

temp_root.description: The single absolute root every arm's disposable profile, cache, repository and plugin copy lives under. An arm that writes outside it has left the isolation the design was approved with.

argv.description: Passed to the launcher verbatim. No shell, no interpolation: a template expanded at run time is an argv nobody approved.

environment.description: The complete literal environment for this arm. Inheriting the executor's environment would carry credentials the approval never mentioned.

output.description: Where this arm's raw bytes and its host-generated attestation land. Both are no-clobber: an arm that overwrites is an arm that can be re-run until it agrees.
